p: The German Confederation, dominated by Austria, had been dissolved in the Revolutions of 1848 and partially succeeded by the Frankfurt Assembly. After the assembly failed, Prussia took the initiative in early 1850 with the Erfurt Union, a federation of most of the German states under its own lead. The two powers were thus in conflict over the leadership of Germany.

A dispute between the Elector of Hesse and his subjects gave the Austrian chancellor Felix zu Schwarzenberg the occasion to isolate Prussia further. Austrian and allied armies advanced into the Electorate of Hesse, and on 8 November 1850 the Prussian army came close to war with Bavaria, an ally of Austria, near Fulda-Bronnzell. In the Warsaw negotiations of October 1850 Tsar Nicholas I of Russia had already taken Austria's side, which was part of the reason why Prussia decided to give in.

The agreement, also called the Agreement of Olmütz, came out of a conference held in the town, now Olomouc in the Czech Republic, and closed the Autumn Crisis of 1850. Prussia gave up its claim to lead the German states and submitted to Austrian leadership of the restored confederation. It agreed to demobilise, to take part in the intervention of the German Diet in Hesse and in Holstein, and renounced any resumption of the Erfurt Union. Austria for its part agreed to call a conference of ministers to discuss a reform of the confederation.

The ministerial conference that Austria had promised met in Dresden the following year and ended without result, so that the confederation continued unreformed under Austrian leadership. The name of humiliation was given to the treaty because many saw in it a capitulation of the Prussians to the Austrians.

'so that the confederation continued unreformed' is my reading of 'took place in Dresden the following year without result'; cut the clause if too much.
